title: answer an employee question through an authorized retrieval tool
input: The employee asks a bounded question and the application selects its permitted agent configuration.
action: Agent Service coordinates the configured model and supported tools for the agent. Retrieval or action tools use their assigned identities; the application limits data scope and validates tool authorization.
output: The application presents the retrieved answer with available evidence and routes unsupported actions for approval.
check: Test tool denial, prompt injection, run failure and cross-user data isolation before release.

title: govern model and agent deployments before application release
input: The platform owner selects the actual supported Foundry project, deployment and governance controls.
action: The configured Foundry management capabilities govern supported model or agent resources and their access or policy settings. The runtime deployment executes inference; the control configuration bounds how applications can use it.
output: The application team releases only the approved deployment and records its model, identity and policy settings.
check: Verify effective permissions, policy enforcement and the actual runtime behavior rather than relying on a dashboard label.

title: retrieve enterprise knowledge for an authorized agent answer
input: The agent application supplies a bounded question and configured enterprise knowledge sources.
action: Foundry IQ's supported knowledge capabilities connect and retrieve information from configured sources. Identity, connector scope and source permissions determine accessible evidence; application code validates the generated response.
output: The agent presents permitted citations or source results to the employee for the requested task.
check: Test source ACLs, stale content, irrelevant retrieval and unavailable connectors before enabling enterprise answers.

title: invoke an approved model deployment for document classification
input: The application submits permitted document content with a validated output schema.
action: The selected Foundry model deployment performs the supported inference operation using its configured endpoint and model settings. Deployment access and model capabilities bound the request; the application validates the classification.
output: The document handler accepts supported labels and queues uncertain output for review.
check: Evaluate representative classes, invalid output, model-version changes and input privacy before production use.

title: compose an application with a selected language analysis API
input: The developer chooses the actual supported tool API and approved input scope.
action: The selected Foundry tool provides its documented operation, such as language extraction, speech recognition or vision analysis. The application calls that specific API and interprets its response; the tool collection is not one universal processor.
output: The application uses the validated tool response for its defined business task and handles unsupported inputs explicitly.
check: Test the chosen API's schema, permissions, error behavior and quality against task-specific samples.

title: triage repository security findings before release
input: The maintainer enables the permitted code, dependency and secret-scanning features for the repository.
action: Advanced Security's configured scanners identify supported code vulnerabilities, dependency alerts or secret exposure. Repository policy determines required checks; developers investigate findings and rotate real exposed credentials.
output: The release owner accepts the repaired revision after required security checks and application tests pass.
check: Verify alert applicability, fix coverage and secret revocation without assuming dismissal removes a vulnerability.

service: GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps
title: gate an Azure repository change on validated security findings
input: The maintainer configures supported security scanning for the approved Azure DevOps repository.
action: The security integration analyzes supported code, dependencies and secrets under its configured checks. Findings inform release decisions; application owners validate exploitability and fix confirmed issues.
output: The Azure pipeline promotes only the revision meeting its configured security and quality gates.
check: Test scanning coverage, pull-request checks, finding permissions and remediation validation before enforcing the gate.

title: implement a reviewed testable feature with coding assistance
input: The developer supplies approved repository context and the requested feature requirements.
action: Copilot assists with supported code completion and development tasks in the configured environment. Suggested code remains a proposed change; the developer checks behavior, dependency use and repository policy.
output: The maintainer reviews the diff and submits it through normal build, test and pull-request gates.
check: Verify acceptance requirements, secret handling and unintended code changes before merging assisted implementation.

title: control a repository release through enterprise access policy
input: The organization assigns repository roles and defines the approved branch and release controls.
action: GitHub Enterprise provides the organization's configured source collaboration and enterprise policy capabilities. Repository workflows build or deploy code only when configured; enterprise access governs who can trigger or approve them.
output: The release owner promotes the reviewed commit with linked workflow and approval evidence.
check: Test branch protection, workflow credentials, offboarding and deployment approvals using the intended enterprise policy.

title: run a supported distributed analytical job over enterprise data
input: The engineer selects a supported cluster type, job code and authorized storage dataset.
action: HDInsight supplies the selected supported distributed analytics cluster. Spark or other configured engine workers execute the submitted job; cluster compatibility and data permissions govern successful processing.
output: The job writes accepted output partitions for the reporting consumer.
check: Check supported engine versions, partition counts, retry behavior and required cluster lifecycle migration before scheduling production.
